proposed_from.topic: Sharp full-law recovery modulus at Morse-critical circular interventions. On bounded C^k causal models over T^n with grouped positive single-node perfect interventions, define complete-family Hellinger distance between observed environment laws and L2 encoder distance modulo node permutations and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms. Under a finite order-m derivative profile, prove the matching inverse modulus Omega_km(eps) asymptotic to eps^((k+1)/(k+m+1)), with the primary C2/Morse exponent 3/4, uniformly over both DAGs, mechanisms, and decoders. Treat CauCA plateau rotations and Varici et al. almost-everywhere exact recovery as occupied. Give a certified Fourier/spline recovery and confidence-set rung. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Multiplying every node-target baseline density and dividing by observational density^(n-1) exactly yields the decoder pushforward of an independent baseline product for any DAG. After coordinate probability-integral gauges this controls determinant error, while within-group ratios control factorization residuals, without losing the Hellinger exponent under two-sided nuisance variation. For bounded radial Hamiltonian twists, angular averaging plus interpolation through the critical hole proves the matching exponent; conditional variance of exp(i T_i) prevents quotient absorption. In the two-node C2/Morse family, exact expansions give representation error h^3 and full-law Hellinger error h^4. Ratio-only strip alternatives yield a worse exponent but incur determinant error and are excluded by the synthetic law. Checks covered anisotropic and oscillatory packets, winding, positivity, flat and coalescing critical regimes, quotient absorption, and current nonlinear/linear recovery literature; no full-modulus collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the degenerate incompressible-rigidity inequality for arbitrary bounded C2 torus diffeomorphisms in the two-node Morse model, then extend it uniformly over both nuisance classes. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove or refute the normalized divergence-free C2 inequality using joint-critical and oscillatory-strip packets; any unbounded sequence or need for extra critical-spacing/decoder assumptions pivots the run. seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 1--2; Theorem 4.2, p. 5; proof in Appendix B.2, pp. 18--21; plateau construction in Appendix C, p. 27; Discussion, p. 10.
seed_details.question: Does complete-family Hellinger error \(\varepsilon\) force quotient encoder error of exact order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\) on the full bounded \(C^2\) two-node torus class when every intervention log-ratio has Morse critical points?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The exact CauCA proof differentiates an equality and divides by an almost-everywhere nonzero discrepancy. The first changed step replaces division near isolated zeros by a weighted coercivity inequality that uses the synthetic determinant equation to control the divergence-free remainder.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{CauCA}+\text{Hellinger modulus}+\text{Morse criticality}\), \(\text{nonlinear causal representation}+3/4\), and \(\text{intervention law stability}+\text{torus diffeomorphism}\) found qualitative identification, plateau failures, and near-isometry robustness, but no matching full-law modulus.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Liang et al. because their almost-everywhere discrepancy already implies componentwise recovery.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their proof is qualitative and divides exact score identities by the discrepancy; it gives no stability when the derivative approaches zero, while their counterexample uses a positive-measure plateau rather than isolated Morse zeros.

seed_details.anchor_read: Overview, pp. 2--4; Definition 21, p. 28; Theorem 22 and equations (79)--(82), pp. 29--30; Theorem 25, pp. 31--32; Discussion, pp. 49--50.
seed_details.question: For an order-\(m\) zero and \(C^k\) decoder regularity, is the sharp inverse exponent exactly \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\), and is finite-order criticality the boundary between Hölder stability and plateau nonidentification?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Varici et al. infer zero cross-Jacobian entries from a zero score-loss integrand and a discrepancy that is nonzero off a null set. The first changed step is a sublevel-set and interpolation estimate that quantifies how much mixed displacement can hide where the discrepancy derivative is small.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing finite-type or Łojasiewicz exponents with nonlinear ICA, score diversity, and causal representation recovery found quantitative Morse geometry but no causal inverse-modulus theorem.
seed_details.red_team: A standard Hölder interpolation inequality mechanically yields the exponent once the derivative has order \(m\).
seed_details.rebuttal: Scalar interpolation alone misses volume-preserving transverse motions and two-sided profile nuisance; the exponent requires coupling the determinant residual, factorization residuals, and the quotient by coordinate diffeomorphisms, with a matching legal lower family.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 1--2; Theorems 1--4, pp. 8--9; proof interface in Appendix, pp. 26--29; Conclusion, p. 10.
seed_details.question: Can simultaneous torus density bands and a certified periodic sieve produce an honest confidence set for the nonlinear encoder equivalence class whose diameter is the density-law rate raised to the critical inverse exponent?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Acartürk et al. propagate generic score-estimation error through linear subspace perturbation. The first changed step is to replace matrix perturbation by a complete-family Hellinger confidence ball and propagate it through a nonregular quotient modulus.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for nonlinear interventional causal representation confidence sets, quotient \(L^2\) coverage, and torus Fourier Hellinger recovery found manifold density bands and generic \(L^2\) confidence-set theory, but no encoder-quotient construction.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine plug-in corollary of a density estimator and the population modulus.
seed_details.rebuttal: Coverage must be simultaneous over environments and survive sieve approximation, global torus invertibility, quotient minimization, and a Hölder rather than differentiable inverse; the known-order nonadaptive construction is feasible, while adaptation has a separate honesty obstruction.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 2--4; Theorem 3.1 and proof, pp. 12--13; Theorem 3.4, p. 14; Hellinger corollaries, p. 18.
seed_details.question: Does a normalized divergence-free \(C^2\) field on \(\mathbb T^2\) satisfy the weighted \(3/4\)-coercivity inequality induced by two transverse Morse profiles, or can an oscillatory packet violate it and integrate to a full-law counterexample?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Khesin et al. identify density space as a quotient by volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. The first changed step is to add coordinate-specific weighted transport equations and prove they are coercive on the invisible vertical tangent space.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining incompressible rigidity, weighted scalar transport, Morse weights, and torus Hellinger geometry found no such coercivity theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This is an analysis lemma with no causal content and follows from geometric rigidity.
seed_details.rebuttal: Friesecke--James--Müller controls distance of a Jacobian from \(SO(n)\); here the defects are determinant error and degenerate weighted scalar equations, and the lemma is exactly the missing causal stability step.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 1--2; Theorem 3.1, p. 5; proof through the quantitative Sard, inverse-function, and Morse steps, pp. 5--10.
seed_details.question: What replacement modulus holds when isolated critical points coalesce or when the critical set becomes a submanifold of positive dimension?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The quantitative Morse theorem isolates uniformly nondegenerate critical neighborhoods. The first changed step is to translate the sublevel-tube geometry of non-Morse profiles into the volume available to localized incompressible encoder motions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for critical-submanifold geometry paired with causal representation moduli found no occupied result; nearby work treats critical values of smooth maps, not causal law families.
seed_details.red_team: The answer is just the codimension of the critical set inserted into a standard sublevel-volume calculation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The incompressibility constraint couples different critical strips and can change the packet geometry, so codimension alone does not determine the law-to-quotient exponent.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction and Theorem 1, pp. 2--4; deformation proof, pp. 9--12; nonuniqueness by radial volume-preserving rotations, p. 2.
seed_details.question: Can the product of all target-baseline observed densities divided by the observational density to power \(n-1\) canonically separate volume correction from causal factorization for arbitrary DAGs and nuisance mechanisms?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Dacorogna--Moser solves the prescribed-Jacobian equation but leaves a volume-preserving kernel. The first changed step is an exact causal factor-cancellation identity producing the relevant pushed-forward product law before applying any Jacobian correction.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for this exact complete-intervention density product in CauCA and score-based CRL did not locate it as a named theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The identity is immediate algebra from truncated factorization and cannot support a paper by itself.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds as to standalone ambition; the identity remains essential because it rules out ratio-only strip alternatives and enables nuisance-uniform determinant control.

seed_details.anchor_read: Theorem 1 and the explicit nonunique disk rotations, pp. 2--3; deformation construction, pp. 9--12.
seed_details.question: Can support-localized Hamiltonian twists at a joint finite-order critical point furnish a fixed-class lower bound that survives the full coordinatewise quotient?
seed_details.proof_boundary: The prescribed-Jacobian literature supplies localized volume correction but not a causal indistinguishability calculation. The first changed step is to scale a radial Hamiltonian twist so its \(C^k\) norm stays bounded and compute every intervention-law Hellinger expansion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing localized prescribed-Jacobian maps with intervention-density lower bounds found no target-method collision.
seed_details.red_team: CauCA already uses distance-dependent determinant-one rotations.
seed_details.rebuttal: CauCA's rotation lies on a common positive-measure plateau and gives exact nonidentification; the localized family has only isolated finite-order critical points, nonzero law error, an exact scaling frontier, and a quotient lower bound via conditional variance.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 1--3; Theorem 4.1, p. 6; rigidity proof in Appendix E, pp. 20--22; Conclusion, p. 9.
seed_details.question: When do near-isometry defect and complete-law Hellinger defect yield equivalent representation guarantees, and where does determinant-only control diverge because of the incompressible coset?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Buchholz and Schölkopf feed distance of the decoder Jacobian from rotations directly into geometric rigidity. The first changed step is to derive an observable defect from environment laws and characterize the frontier at which it controls the full map rather than only its density coset.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for equivalence between near-isometry and intervention-law robustness found no observable threshold connecting the two defects.
seed_details.red_team: This merely rephrases geometric rigidity under a different norm.
seed_details.rebuttal: The law defect controls only determinant and coordinate-weighted residuals, not distance to rotations; equivalence would require a new causal coercivity frontier and may fail outside the complete family.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, pp. 1--2; population proof summary, p. 4; Theorem 3.8 and proof sketch, pp. 6--7; detailed numerical-differentiation proof, pp. 15--16; Conclusion, p. 9.
seed_details.question: Can numerical differentiation of intervention density ratios deliver a finite-sample quotient recovery guarantee at Morse zeros without estimating full environment densities?
seed_details.proof_boundary: Lyu and Fu propagate regression error into cross-derivative error under global variability. The first changed step is a spatially adaptive derivative estimate whose bandwidth expands through critical holes while retaining determinant information from the baseline product.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-sample nonlinear ICA with Morse-degenerate score diversity found only globally conditioned variability results.
seed_details.red_team: Lyu and Fu's numerical differentiation proof transfers directly after replacing the auxiliary variable by the intervention label.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their full-rank variability matrix is uniformly conditioned and their loss controls a different mixed-derivative diagnostic; finite-order score zeros create a nonregular quotient inverse and require the missing determinant channel.
